Yes. Monzo can temporarily freeze or restrict a UK account while it checks unusual activity, protects you from suspected fraud, or carries out legally required checks. A review doesn’t necessarily mean you’ve done anything wrong, and Monzo may not be able to tell you exactly what triggered it. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/account-and-profile/your-account-is-under-review))

**If it happens:**

1. **Check the Monzo app.** It will tell you which restrictions apply. For example, transfers might be blocked while some card payments still work. Monzo also sends updates and requests for documents through the app; reply there promptly if it asks for anything. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/account-and-profile/your-account-is-under-review))
2. **If you can’t pay for essentials, don’t wait for an update.** Use in-app chat and tell support exactly what you need to pay for and when. For example: *“My account is under review and I need £25 for medication today. What help is available?”* Urgent support is available **24/7**. If you can’t access the app, **call Monzo free from the UK on 0800 088 4040**. For help getting back into the app, you can also email **help@monzo.com**. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/account-and-profile/your-account-is-under-review))
3. **If you’re unhappy with how Monzo handles it, make a formal complaint** in the app or email **complaints@monzo.com**. Keep a record of missed payments or charges. If Monzo’s final response doesn’t resolve it, or it doesn’t respond in time, you can take the complaint to the **Financial Ombudsman Service** for free. You normally have **six months from the date of Monzo’s final response** to do so. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/legal-stuff/make-complaint-web?utm_source=openai))
